video_title: Felix Zulauf: One More Rally Left Before Major Market Correction Next Year
gist: Felix Zulauf expects the current correction to bottom near S&P 7,100/Nasdaq 100 ~26,000, followed by a final rally above 8,000 into a Q1-Q2 2027 high, then a liquidity-driven panic (up to 50% for the Nasdaq 100) that forces a 'mother of all stimulations' and a run toward S&P 10,000 before a 2030s systemic crisis. He favors building duration now (Bunds/JGBs for a falling dollar), buying gold below $4,000, and turning defensive from early 2027.

themes.theme: Near-term bottom then final rally to S&P 8,000+

insights.claim: Felix Zulauf expects the current correction to bottom around S&P 7,100 (range 6,900-7,200, 'very low 7,000s') and Nasdaq 100 near or slightly below 26,000, by late 2026 or possibly extending into January.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Defines a buy zone for equities; a decisive break well below ~6,900 would invalidate his medium-term bottom call.
insights.quote: I said we will probably uh see the S&P declining into the range 6900 7200 or so. and uh 7,100 would be my ballpark uh target

insights.claim: Sentiment has shifted from complacency to fear and aggressive money has largely liquidated AI and tech stocks, which Zulauf views as a constructive setup for a medium-term bottom.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Fear and liquidation of crowded AI positions are a contrarian buy signal rather than evidence the AI cycle is over.
insights.quote: I think the aggressive money is to a very large extent out of the AI stocks and technology in in general and I think that's very good

insights.claim: Zulauf rejects the view that the AI bubble has burst; he sees the current decline as a correction within an AI investment cycle that runs from the 2022 bottom to a top around 2027.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Treat the AI selloff as a cyclical shakeout, not a cycle end, until the projected 2027 peak.
insights.quote: Most people believe the AI bubble has burst and the AI cycle is over. I'm I'm not so sure

insights.claim: From the coming medium-term bottom, Zulauf expects a rally to new S&P highs above 8,000 peaking in late Q1 or early Q2 2027, which he calls the last rally before the cycle's biggest shakeout.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Position long into early 2027 but plan to de-risk around the late-Q1/early-Q2 high.
insights.quote: I expect a rally back up uh potentially to new highs above 8,000. But that is in my view the last rally for the biggest shakeout in this cycle

insights.claim: Nvidia has already hit Zulauf's ~$150 downside target, is ahead of the pack in the down cycle, and could rise 50-100% over the next six months.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Nvidia is his top-down candidate for the sharpest rebound off the medium-term bottom.
insights.quote: I wouldn't be surprised to see Nvidia up 50 to 100% uh uh over the next 6 months or so

insights.claim: Zulauf's track record cited in-episode: in April 2025 he called the bottom and projected S&P ~7,500 when many thought he was wrong, and he forecast 10-year yields reaching 5.25-5.5%, which has occurred.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Context for weighting his calls: prior targets on equities and bond yields were hit.

themes.theme: 2027 panic decline, mega-stimulus and final blow-off

insights.claim: After the early-2027 high, Zulauf expects a financial-system liquidity squeeze to trigger a correction that, because the S&P is concentrated in a few megacaps (~40% of the index; tech >50%), could deepen from 20% to 30% and up to 50% for the Nasdaq 100.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Index concentration amplifies downside; reduce megacap tech exposure into the Q2 2027 high.
insights.quote: A 20% correction could then easily turn into a 30% correction and maybe even 50% correction for the NASDAQ 100

insights.claim: Zulauf likens the expected 2027 decline to the 1998 panic during the dotcom boom: a shock within an ongoing investment cycle rather than the end of it.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Use the 1998 LTCM-style panic-then-rally template rather than a 2000-style bust for 2027.

insights.claim: Once stocks are down ~20%, Zulauf expects authorities to respond with larger deficits and very easy money—'the mother of all stimulations'—in late 2027/early 2028.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Watch for policy capitulation after a 20%+ drawdown as the signal to re-risk aggressively.
insights.quote: I think we could see in late 27, early 28 the mother of all stimulations kick in

insights.claim: Zulauf's path: S&P low around 5,000 in late 2027/early 2028, then a one-to-two-year stimulus-fueled run to roughly 10,000 that ends a multi-generational cycle dating from 1974 or 1932.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Implies a ~doubling from the stimulus low; the subsequent top could be a secular peak.
insights.quote: So the low for me in late 27, early 28 is perhaps S&P 5,000 and uh and then another uh one to twoyear run to maybe 10,000

insights.claim: Zulauf's suggested playbook: be long equities (especially tech) through the Q2 2027 high, then shift to the most defensive, non-cyclical equities possible from the first months of 2027, hold cash/duration/gold through the panic, and re-buy broadly once stimulus arrives.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: A dated regime-rotation plan: risk-on now, defensive from early 2027, risk-on again after the stimulus announcement.
insights.quote: I would go to the most defensive character that is possible um and and not not cyclical stuff

insights.claim: At the next bottom Zulauf would decide leadership by how assets behaved during the decline, noting tech could lead again but declining to recommend anything yet.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Relative strength during the drawdown is his screen for the post-stimulus leaders.

themes.theme: Rates, bonds and the secular rise in yields

insights.claim: Zulauf told subscribers 10-year yields are topping near 5.25-5.5%, arguing the bond market itself is forcing the AI investment boom to slow.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Peak yields are the mechanism slowing capex; a top in yields marks the turn toward a duration trade.
insights.quote: it's the bond market that is pushing for a slowdown of the investment boom and that's happening

insights.claim: Zulauf expects 10-year yields to fall 150-200 basis points over the next ~12 months (to a 3-handle), which he calls the first temporary cyclical correction within a secular uptrend in yields.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Build long duration now to capture price gains as yields fall into the 2027 equity panic.
insights.quote: the decline in bond yields next year from the current high or so for the next 12 months probably by 150 to 200 basis points is the first temporary cyclical correction in a rising yield trend

insights.claim: Deglobalization, wars, protectionism and sanctions are inflationary, so the 40-year decline in rates is over and rates and inflation are now in a secular uptrend; authorities can no longer stimulate freely.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Duration is a cyclical trade, not a secular hold; structural inflation caps how long bonds work.

insights.claim: Inflation is a lagging indicator; with oil reversing lower, Zulauf expects inflation to fall cyclically from ~4% to a new floor of around 3%, giving bonds relief.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: A cyclical disinflation supports the near-term bond rally even as the secular floor rises.
insights.quote: the new level is 3% or so. So, we go back down from four to 3%

insights.claim: Contrary to mainstream media, Zulauf says rising bond yields and rising stock prices are normal during most of a cycle; they diverge only at late and early stages.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Don't read rising yields alone as bearish for stocks; watch for the late-cycle divergence.
insights.quote: Rising bond yields and rising stock prices is a normal occurrence. It's different from what they tell you in all the um newspapers

insights.claim: Starting from late 2027, Zulauf expects 10-year yields to break decisively above 5-5.5% and potentially reach ~8% globally, a level a record-leveraged system cannot handle, causing a market-driven systemic crisis.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: The post-stimulus bond selloff is the key risk that ends the cycle; exit duration before late 2027.
insights.quote: We could easily go to 8% or so

insights.claim: Zulauf expects the first half of the 2030s to bring major disruption, systemic crisis and several sovereign debt defaults, with protecting capital paramount from about 2030 onward.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Long-horizon investors should plan for a capital-preservation regime in the 2030s.
insights.quote: With with with several with with several governments defaulting on their debt

themes.theme: Dollar breakdown and non-US bond trade

insights.claim: Zulauf prefers 10-year German Bunds and 10-year Japanese government bonds over Treasuries for USD-based investors, because falling yields there would compound with currency gains when the US stock market breaks.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Express the duration trade unhedged in EUR and JPY bonds to add an FX kicker.
insights.quote: It's even better if you go to German boons, 10 year German boons or 10-year Japanese government bonds because there you will also make a currency gain

insights.claim: Current-account-surplus nations have recycled surpluses via sovereign wealth funds into US AI/tech stocks rather than Treasuries, at record levels; a big 2027 equity decline would trigger outflows that pressure the dollar.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Foreign ownership of US tech is the transmission channel from an equity crash to a dollar crash.
insights.quote: they have invested through their sovereign wealth funds in AI stocks

insights.claim: The US dollar index has been in an uptrend channel since 2008; Zulauf expects a major downside break in 2027 with heavy selling versus Asian and European currencies.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Watch the 2008 channel's lower bound as the trigger for a structural dollar short.

insights.claim: Zulauf says the preferred collateral of central banks in a crisis is gold, not US Treasuries, and gold is now the largest central-bank reserve asset, larger than Treasuries.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Central-bank reserve shift signals declining trust in government debt and structural gold demand.
insights.quote: Gold is now the largest asset of central banks in their reserves larger than US treasuries

insights.claim: Zulauf cites news that Hong Kong has overtaken Switzerland as the number-one offshore financial center, reading it as offshore investors trusting China's government more than Western democracies.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Signals capital migration away from Western financial centers amid eroding trust.

insights.claim: Gold peaked at $5,595 in January, fell to the mid-4,000s, bounced to ~5,400, and Zulauf now sees it in buying territory between $3,800 and $4,000, with ~$3,800 the ideal entry.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Accumulate gold below $4,000, scaling in nearer $3,800.
insights.quote: between 3800 and 4,000 and um the better you can buy it closer to 3,800 the better it is

insights.claim: Zulauf expects gold to rally about 50% next year to roughly $6,000 under his scenario, and potentially toward ~$10,000 by the late stage of the stimulus-driven equity boom, when gold should outperform equities.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Gold is a core holding through both the 2027 panic and the subsequent liquidity boom.
insights.quote: I expect gold to rally 50% or so next year

insights.claim: Silver below $50 (target $44-46) is a long-term buy; it is in roughly its seventh year of production deficit and could outperform gold on the upside, though it is more volatile and is an industrial rather than monetary metal.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Use silver as a higher-beta complement to gold, sized for volatility.

insights.claim: At high silver prices the world's largest solar-panel maker in China began switching from silver to copper, a long-term overhang, but with silver back below $50 Zulauf thinks the incentive to substitute has faded.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Thrifting in solar caps silver upside at high prices; watch substitution announcements.

insights.claim: Zulauf would include gold mining stocks alongside physical gold in his buy recommendation.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Miners offer leverage to the gold call.

insights.claim: In a late-cycle systemic dislocation (late 2020s/early 2030s), liquidity squeezes pull gold, silver and all commodities down too; the goal then is to 'lose the least'.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Gold is not immune in a liquidity crisis; hold liquidity and relative-loss mindset.
insights.quote: those who lose the least will be the king

insights.claim: Zulauf expects commodities broadly to be in a bear market over the next 12 months, then become a fantastic place to be once the mega-stimulus arrives.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Underweight commodities now; rotate in after the stimulus signal.

insights.claim: Zulauf sees Bitcoin as a trading vehicle, not an investment: after dropping below 70,000 it should bottom and rally to ~100,000 in the first half of 2027, then could fall to ~40,000 after the Q2 equity high.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Trade Bitcoin with equity risk; he expects it to track the 2027 panic.
insights.quote: Bitcoin could go from 100,000 to 40,000 thereafter

insights.claim: Zulauf warns Bitcoin's fixed supply is attractive, but governments seeking control in a crisis could declare it illegal, which would make it worthless if big governments do so.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Regulatory/ban risk is the key long-term tail for Bitcoin versus physical gold.
insights.quote: if the big governments declare it as illegal it's worth nothing

themes.theme: AI capex overbuild and 2028 earnings risk

insights.claim: Zulauf says the AI buildout is the largest US investment boom ever—bigger than railroads, the internet or computers—pushing the economy to near full capacity and straining credit.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Credit demand from AI is the driver of high rates and the eventual slowdown.
insights.quote: bigger than the railroads bigger than the internet bigger than the computer

insights.claim: Hyperscalers' free cash flow has collapsed as they fund AI buildouts with debt and equity issuance, and shareholders have pushed back by selling the stocks.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Watch hyperscaler FCF and capital raising as the gauge of capex fatigue.
insights.quote: Free cash flow of the large investors in AI, the hypers scalers has declined like a stone

insights.claim: 2027 tech earnings should hold up because orders are signed, but 2028 is the problem: semiconductor capacity expansions coming on stream from 2028 will push chip prices, earnings estimates and margins down.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Semis are the most exposed sub-sector to the 2028 earnings cliff; markets may start discounting it in 2027.
insights.quote: 28 I think is the problem for the tax sector when new capacity comes on stream in semiconductor industry

insights.claim: Tech-sector earnings excluding the six biggest companies are up ~100% with profit margins around 70%, which Zulauf calls an unsustainable temporary boom.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Margin mean-reversion is the core downside risk to tech earnings.

insights.claim: Zulauf's framework for tech booms: overbuild capacity, prices of the service fall, early investors' returns collapse and some fail, then the economy grows into the technology over ~20 years with productivity around a ~1% trend; AI is no different.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Expect the AI productivity payoff over decades, not to rescue near-term returns on capex.
insights.quote: I think this investment boom in this new technology is no different than all the others

themes.theme: Multipolar geopolitics, oil and capital controls

insights.claim: Zulauf argues the West has lost its dominance for the first time in 500 years and the world is in 'multipolar disorder' with conflict, protectionism and sanctions, an inflationary backdrop.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Supports structurally higher inflation, rates and hard-asset demand.
insights.quote: We are in a multipolar disorder

insights.claim: Zulauf believes Iran is now number two or three in missile technology after Russia, can destroy Middle East oil infrastructure, and the US cannot win militarily; he expects a renewed war and Strait of Hormuz closure later in the 2020s sending oil to $200.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Long-dated oil upside tail; Middle East energy infrastructure is at risk.
insights.quote: then I see oil at $200

insights.claim: Until a major escalation, Zulauf expects oil to swing between ~$60 and $110 on news flow, currently trending down toward ~$60, with the Strait open about 70-80%; the US is short ammunition, diesel and jet fuel, limiting it to tit-for-tat strikes.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Range-trade oil near-term; the falling oil price supports the disinflation/bond call.

insights.claim: Zulauf expects Russia to win the Ukraine war, viewing it as a US proxy conflict, and sees a trend toward spheres of influence, citing Venezuela as an effort to keep Western Hemisphere resources in US hands.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Spheres-of-influence world implies regional resource blocs and persistent sanctions risk.

insights.claim: Zulauf says China's published growth numbers are fake and it suffers classic planned-economy overinvestment, dumping excess capacity as exports that squeeze Western margins and drive tariffs and protectionism.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Chinese overcapacity is a persistent margin headwind for Western manufacturers and a tariff driver.

insights.claim: Zulauf expects capital controls and possible confiscations (as with Russian assets) in coming years and advises keeping savings in a familiar jurisdiction rather than peripheral markets.
insights.speaker: Felix Zulauf
insights.so_what: Jurisdiction risk matters: avoid offshore/peripheral structures where funds could be trapped.
insights.quote: There will certainly be capital controls
